question.text: Let the tangent and normal at any point $P\left(at^2\right.$, 2at), $(a > 0)$, on the parabola $y^2=4 a x$ meet the axis of the parabola at $T$ and $\mathrm{G}$ respectively. Then the radius of the circle through $\mathrm{P}, \mathrm{T}$ and $\mathrm{G}$ is

solution.text:
$P\left(a t^2, 2 a t\right), T\left(-a t^2, 0\right), G\left(2 a+a t^2, 0\right)$
Slope of $P T \times$ Slope of $P G=-1$
$\therefore$ TG is a diameter of the circle through points $\mathrm{P}, \mathrm{T}$ and $\mathrm{G}$.
$\therefore \text { radius }=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{TG}=\mathrm{a}\left(1+\mathrm{t}^2\right)$
